instruction: Look at turned_shaft.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. Create a Turning CAM-Part for turned_shaft.step with the SOLIDWORKS CAM Turning module; do not model this shaft as a 3-axis Milling CAM-Part. Use the shaft centerline as the turning Z axis and use a turning coordinate system that posts X/Z turning moves only, with no Y-axis milling motion in the NC program. Set the stock to fully enclose the shaft using SOLIDWORKS CAM's automatic or standard turning stock setup. Program standard turning operations for rough turning, finish turning, grooving, and center drilling or spot drilling of the shaft end. Use suitable installed roughing, finishing, grooving, and center-drill or spot-drill tools; exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, and internal tool-library IDs may follow stable SOLIDWORKS CAM Technology Database defaults. Keep SOLIDWORKS CAM's default generated NC comments; do not rename operations just to add labels. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-16.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For this turning task, use an installed turning .ctl post such as fanuc_t2axis.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s). Do not manually write, fabricate, or directly create the NC/G-code text outside SOLIDWORKS CAM. You must complete all operations interactively through the graphical user interface (GUI) step by step. The use of external script files is strictly prohibited.
